title: Quadriplegia, paraplegia, monoplegia and spinal cord disorders
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's paralysis or spinal cord condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of paraplegia and associated mobility.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his chronic paraplegia. He reports that he suffered a spinal cord injury many years ago, which resulted in his current level of mobility. He states that he is currently stable and has not experienced any new neurological changes or significant changes in his functional status since the last visit. He reports that his current management plan is effective for his daily needs. He denies any new areas of numbness, sharp pain, or sudden weakness. He is able to manage his activities of daily living with the assistance of his current mobility aids.

Medication List
- Gabapentin 300mg TID
- Baclofen 10mg TID
- Oxycodone 5mg every 6 hours as needed for breakthrough pain

Review of Systems
The patient denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations. He denies recent fevers, chills, or night sweats. He denies any new urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits. He reports no new headaches or dizziness. He denies any new visual or auditory changes.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his spouse and receives assistance from a home health aide. He is a former smoker but quit over 30 years ago. He denies any alcohol or illicit drug use.

Family History
Father had hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Mother had osteoarthritis.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.4 F
Blood Pressure: 128/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 97% on room air
Height: 5'10"
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
Glucose: 105 mg/dL
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. He is sitting upright in a wheelchair. Skin is intact and dry. Neurological exam confirms the presence of chronic paraplegia. Reflexes are diminished in the lower extremities. No new motor deficits were noted during today's evaluation.

Assessment
1. Paraplegia due to old spinal cord injury.

Plan
1. Continue current medication regimen for pain and spasticity management.
2. Maintain current mobility aids and home health assistance.
3. Follow up in 6 months for routine evaluation.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
